The first release of EnvoScale: the Envol compiler, built by itself, with the standard library and the `envo` tool.

**Download** `envoscale-0.5.0.tar` and unpack it anywhere (`tar -xf`, which Windows 10 and later also have). `bin/` holds `envo` and `envoc` for Linux and Windows (x86-64); run `bin/envo run hello.envol`. The library sits beside `bin/`, where `envo` finds it.

**What it is.** CI built this archive on Linux and on Windows from the same commit and published it only because both builds were byte-identical. The compiler in it was built by itself, starting from the seed compiler that [EnvoScaleAsm](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScaleAsm) builds from assembly. `envoscale-0.5.0.provenance.json` records the commit, the command and the digests of the compilers that built it; `SHA256SUMS` has the archive's digest.

**Not yet:** the archive is not signed (the project's signing key is not set up), there are no macOS or AArch64 Linux builds of the tools themselves (programs for those targets do build: `--target aarch64-macos`, `--target aarch64-linux`), and everything is Experimental: see [docs/status.md](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScale/blob/main/docs/status.md).
